0-northborough-road-common-driveway.name: 0 Northborough Road common driveway special permit
0-northborough-road-common-driveway.description: Special permit application to allow 15 feet of frontage on an 8-acre parcel to divide the land into two residential building lots served by a common driveway.
0-northborough-road-common-driveway.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted 5-0 to approve a frontage variance allowing an MWRA easement to serve two residential lots on a common driveway and accepted the withdrawal of the companion special permit.

0-southville-road.name: 0 Southville Road apartment development
0-southville-road.description: Proposed construction of two apartment buildings and associated infrastructure at 0 Southville Road.
0-southville-road.status: The Conservation Commission voted 4-0 to continue the Notice of Intent and stormwater management permit hearing for two apartment buildings to a future session.

0-valley-road-trail.name: 0 Valley Road footbridge and trail
0-valley-road-trail.description: Proposed construction of a wooden boardwalk and trail connection on Southborough Open Land Foundation land off Valley Road.
0-valley-road-trail.status: The Conservation Commission voted 4-0 to close the public hearing and 3-0-1 to issue an Order of Conditions with special conditions for the footbridge and trail project on Southborough Open Land Foundation property.

1-overlook-drive-pool.name: 1 Overlook Drive swimming pool
1-overlook-drive-pool.description: Notice of Intent to construct an inground swimming pool, patio, and cabana within the wetland buffer zone at 1 Overlook Drive.
1-overlook-drive-pool.status: The Conservation Commission voted 4-0 to close the public hearing and approve an Order of Conditions with special conditions for the pool, cabana, and patio project at 1 Overlook Drive.

104-boston-road-water-appeal.name: 104 Boston Road water bill appeal
104-boston-road-water-appeal.description: Abatement appeal before the Water Commissioners regarding an underground leak and high water bill at 104 Boston Road.
104-boston-road-water-appeal.status: The Select Board voted 4-0-1 acting as Water Commissioners to grant a partial bill abatement for 104 Boston Road, reducing a $2,872 underground leak bill to $1,100.

14-newton-street.name: 14 Newton Street garage and ADU
14-newton-street.description: Notice of Intent to construct a detached garage with an accessory dwelling unit and replacement septic in the wetland buffer at 14 Newton Street.
14-newton-street.status: The Board of Health voted 2-1 to approve setback variances to replace a failed septic system and accommodate an accessory dwelling unit.

154-turnpike-road.name: 154 Turnpike Road site plan modification
154-turnpike-road.description: Major site plan approval modification and landscaping compliance for commercial development at 154 Turnpike Road.
154-turnpike-road.status: The Planning Board voted 4-0 to continue the site plan modification hearing to October 19, 2026, without testimony and voted 4-0 to extend its statutory action deadline to October 23, 2026.

170-woodland-road-coc.name: 170 Woodland Road Certificate of Compliance
170-woodland-road-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review for pool, patio, and drainage work within wetland resource areas at 170 Woodland Road.
170-woodland-road-coc.status: The Conservation Commission voted 4-0 to issue a Certificate of Compliance for DEP #290-1129 at 170 Woodland Road.

200-turnpike-road.name: 200 Turnpike Road site plan compliance
200-turnpike-road.description: Site plan compliance, occupancy permitting, and landscape performance bonding for a commercial facility at 200 Turnpike Road.
200-turnpike-road.status: The Planning Board voted 5-0 to accept a surety agreement backed by a $30,000 bond for landscaping and recommended the issuance of a permanent certificate of occupancy.

2030-master-plan-update.name: 2030 Master Plan update
2030-master-plan-update.description: Strategy, funding, and consultant selection for updating Southborough's comprehensive Master Plan for 2030.
2030-master-plan-update.status: The Master Plan Implementation Committee finalized recommendations urging the Planning Board to take ownership of the 2030 Master Plan and establish a dedicated committee in 2027, ahead of a joint meeting scheduled for October 19, 2026.

21-coslin-drive-costco.name: 21 Coslin Drive Costco development
21-coslin-drive-costco.description: Site plan and special permit review for a proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco retail warehouse and 30-position gas station at 21 Coslin Drive.
21-coslin-drive-costco.status: Costco Wholesale presented initial site, grading, traffic, and stormwater plans for a proposed 167,000-square-foot warehouse and 30-position fueling station, drawing resident traffic concerns. The Planning Board voted 4-0 to continue the public hearing to October 19, 2026.

21-highland-street-use.name: 21 Highland Street future use
21-highland-street-use.description: Planning for municipal department space allocation, community use, or potential sale of the town-owned building at 21 Highland Street.
21-highland-street-use.status: The Recreation Commission continues evaluating whether to relocate its offices and expand programming at 21 Highland Street once Youth and Family Services transitions to Flagg School.

22-newton-street-variance.name: 22 Newton Street garage variance
22-newton-street-variance.description: Variance petition under Section 174-8.3(D)(3)(b) to construct a detached two-car garage encroaching on side lot line setbacks at 22 Newton Street.
22-newton-street-variance.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted 5-0 to approve the applicant's request to withdraw the garage variance application without prejudice.

22-turnpike-road.name: 22 Turnpike Road site plan modification
22-turnpike-road.description: Site plan modification to expand stormwater infiltration, permit existing patios and a shed, and address sports lighting at 22 Turnpike Road.
22-turnpike-road.status: The Planning Board voted 4-0 to continue the major site plan modification hearing to October 19, 2026, without testimony while a draft decision is finalized.

229-parkerville-road-coc.name: 229 Parkerville Road Certificate of Compliance
229-parkerville-road-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review and buffer zone encroachment resolution for a fenced garden at 229 Parkerville Road.
229-parkerville-road-coc.status: The Conservation Commission reached an agreement to keep an existing split-rail fence in place while requiring removal of trellises in the buffer zone, deferring final action on the Certificate of Compliance until a fall site visit.

250-turnpike-road.name: 250 Turnpike Road 40B development
250-turnpike-road.description: Comprehensive permit application under Chapter 40B for residential development at 250 Turnpike Road.
250-turnpike-road.status: The Conservation Commission voted 4-0 to continue the Notice of Intent hearing for the 32-unit rental townhouse development while peer review by Lucas Environmental is completed.

34-turnpike-road-special-permit.name: 34 Turnpike Road special permit
34-turnpike-road-special-permit.description: Special permit review and zoning compliance for unpermitted construction and renovations exceeding approvals at 34 Turnpike Road.
34-turnpike-road-special-permit.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted 5-0 to approve 1.3 feet of side setback relief on the condition that the Board of Health certifies the property's septic capacity.

355-turnpike-road-coc.name: 355 Turnpike Road Certificate of Compliance
355-turnpike-road-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review, unapproved paving, and stormwater maintenance for a commercial site at 355 Turnpike Road.
355-turnpike-road-coc.status: The Conservation Commission noted no new information regarding the Certificate of Compliance request for 355 Turnpike Road, leaving action tabled pending site cleanup and engineering clarifications.

40-42-central-street.name: 40-42 Central Street site plan compliance
40-42-central-street.description: Resolution of site plan discrepancies, parking configurations, and occupancy permitting for 40-42 Central Street.
40-42-central-street.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals continued the hearing to October 21, 2026, while the applicant completes paving and inspection of required accessible parking spaces.

55-plus-housing-bylaw.name: 55-plus housing zoning bylaw amendment
55-plus-housing-bylaw.description: Proposed zoning bylaw amendment to eliminate caps on age-restricted 55-plus developments and clarify affordability requirements.
55-plus-housing-bylaw.status: The Affordable Housing Trust continued drafting revisions to the 55-plus housing bylaw following consultations with planning staff and the Zoning Board of Appeals. A revised draft is scheduled for review in October 2026 before submission to town counsel ahead of Annual Town Meeting.

6-walker-street-variance.name: 6 Walker Street garage setback variance
6-walker-street-variance.description: Petition to modify a 1965 variance condition and grant a 6.5-foot side setback variance to construct a garage addition at 6 Walker Street.
6-walker-street-variance.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted 4-0 to modify a 1965 variance restriction and grant a 6.5-foot side setback variance allowing a residential garage addition.

65c-school-street-coc.name: 65C School Street Certificate of Compliance
65c-school-street-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review following unpermitted brush clearing and wetland buffer zone remediation at 65C School Street.
65c-school-street-coc.status: The Conservation Commission voted 4-0 to approve a Certificate of Compliance for 65C School Street following native shrub plantings and lawn restoration in the 20-foot wetland buffer.

66-breakneck-hill-road-variance.name: 66 Breakneck Hill Road septic variance
66-breakneck-hill-road-variance.description: Septic system upgrade and wetland setback variance to support converting a commercial building to residential use at 66 Breakneck Hill Road.
66-breakneck-hill-road-variance.status: The Board of Health voted unanimously to approve a septic variance with an upgraded treatment unit for 66 Breakneck Hill Road, contingent on Conservation Commission approval.

7-turnpike-road-bodywork-compliance.name: 7 Turnpike Road bodywork compliance
7-turnpike-road-bodywork-compliance.description: Town bodywork permitting compliance and cease-and-desist enforcement for an unlicensed massage business operating at 7 Turnpike Road.
7-turnpike-road-bodywork-compliance.status: The Board of Health voted 3-0 to deny an establishment license application for Jojo Bodywork and directed staff and town counsel to execute a written decision.

8-partridge-hill-road-variance.name: 8 Partridge Hill Road septic variance
8-partridge-hill-road-variance.description: Septic repair variance regarding groundwater separation and setback to the Sudbury Reservoir at 8 Partridge Hill Road.
8-partridge-hill-road-variance.status: The Board of Health voted 3-0 to approve septic variances reducing groundwater separation and the reservoir setback for 8 Partridge Hill Road.

911-field-bond-and-fees.name: 911 Field bond repayment and fees
911-field-bond-and-fees.description: Debt service repayment schedule and revolving fund athletic field user fees for the 911 Field turf complex.
911-field-bond-and-fees.status: The Recreation Commission reviewed the field bond repayment schedule and deferred action on proposed fall hourly league fee increases pending updated revenue models.

appointed-town-clerk.name: Appointed town clerk transition
appointed-town-clerk.description: Proposal to transition the town clerk from an elected office to an appointed position, including interim clerk appointments.
appointed-town-clerk.status: The Advisory Committee finalized report language supporting Article 1 to make the Town Clerk an appointed position while recommending that future employment contracts include termination-for-cause protections ahead of Special Town Meeting.

board-of-health-body-art-regulations.name: Board of Health body art regulations
board-of-health-body-art-regulations.description: Revisions to municipal body art regulations regarding practitioner training, apprenticeships, and prohibited activities.
board-of-health-body-art-regulations.status: The Board of Health unanimously adopted revised body art regulations updating practitioner training and apprenticeship standards and explicitly prohibiting vaping in procedure areas.

breakneck-hill-restoration.name: Breakneck Hill Conservation Land restoration
breakneck-hill-restoration.description: Planning and invasive species management for a comprehensive five-zone ecological restoration at Breakneck Hill Conservation Land.
breakneck-hill-restoration.status: The Stewardship Committee is developing a comprehensive five-zone ecological restoration plan with the town planner and voted 4-0 to appoint Freddie Gillespie as committee liaison to the invasive plant contractor.

brox-asphalt-plant-complaints.name: Brox asphalt plant complaints
brox-asphalt-plant-complaints.description: Intermunicipal response and MassDEP oversight regarding resident noise and odor complaints concerning the Brox Industries asphalt plant in Marlborough.
brox-asphalt-plant-complaints.status: MassDEP reported that Brox emissions meet federal standards despite continued resident complaints, and town health staff will continue tracking real-time complaint logs.

cannabis-delivery-opt-out.name: Cannabis delivery opt-out waiver
cannabis-delivery-opt-out.description: Deliberation on whether Southborough should request a state waiver from the Cannabis Control Commission to prohibit adult-use cannabis home delivery.
cannabis-delivery-opt-out.status: A motion to opt out of state regulations allowing adult-use cannabis home delivery failed 1-4 before the Select Board, leaving licensed delivery permitted in Southborough.

cemetery-expansion.name: Town cemetery expansion planning
cemetery-expansion.description: Site evaluation and capacity planning to identify and acquire land for a new municipal cemetery.
cemetery-expansion.status: The Select Board voted 5-0 to formally reduce the Cemetery Expansion Committee charge from five to three members to help achieve quorums.

classification-and-compensation-study.name: Municipal classification and compensation study
classification-and-compensation-study.description: A comprehensive classification and compensation study evaluating 48 non-union municipal employee positions.
classification-and-compensation-study.status: Consultant MGT has gathered compensation survey data from 14 of 18 peer communities and plans to conclude collection within a week ahead of recommendations for the March 2027 Annual Town Meeting.

conservation-land-use-regulations.name: Conservation land use regulations
conservation-land-use-regulations.description: Adoption and amendment of town code regulations governing public use and activities on town-owned conservation land.
conservation-land-use-regulations.status: The Conservation Commission voted 5-0 to formally adopt updated land use regulations for town-owned conservation land under Town Code Section 43-2.

constitution-drive-drainage-and-acceptan.name: Constitution Drive drainage and street acceptance
constitution-drive-drainage-and-acceptan.description: Sinkhole repair at 11 Constitution Drive and resolution of unrecorded municipal street and drainage easements.
constitution-drive-drainage-and-acceptan.status: The Select Board voted unanimously to authorize a one-time $5,000 DPW driveway repair under a homeowner hold-harmless agreement and directed town staff and legal counsel to resolve unrecorded street and drainage easements.

costco-special-act-liquor-license.name: Costco special act liquor license
costco-special-act-liquor-license.description: Proposed special state legislation authorizing an additional off-premises liquor license in Southborough for Costco.
costco-special-act-liquor-license.status: The Select Board agreed to submit a letter of support for refined special legislation that includes a two-year timeline to award the license and a three-year sunset clause, ahead of a State House legislative hearing on June 23, 2026.

culvert-infrastructure-replacements.name: Culvert infrastructure replacements
culvert-infrastructure-replacements.description: Town-wide culvert replacements funded through a state grant to replace previously authorized borrowing.
culvert-infrastructure-replacements.status: The Select Board voted unanimously to accept permanent drainage easements from three Willow Street property owners to advance ongoing culvert replacement work.

downtown-wayfinding-plan.name: Downtown Southborough Wayfinding Plan
downtown-wayfinding-plan.description: A state grant-funded planning study to design and install directional, gateway, and informational signage across downtown Southborough.
downtown-wayfinding-plan.status: The Historical Commission reviewed the draft wayfinding plan and agreed to share feedback with town administration highlighting historic sites and raising concerns over signage clutter.

fay-school-25-middle-road.name: Fay School 25 Middle Road addition
fay-school-25-middle-road.description: Review of as-built plans, construction discrepancies, and landscape mitigation for an addition at Fay School's 25 Middle Road campus.
fay-school-25-middle-road.status: Fay School presented an updated landscape mitigation plan featuring native plantings and a pollinator garden to satisfy prior site plan conditions. The Planning Board continued the discussion to October 19, 2026, pending review of as-built documentation needed for a final certificate of occupancy.

fay-school-athletic-fields.name: Fay School athletic fields redevelopment
fay-school-athletic-fields.description: Notice of Intent and redevelopment to convert grass soccer fields to artificial turf and relocate a baseball field at Fay School's 0 Marlboro Junction property.
fay-school-athletic-fields.status: The Conservation Commission voted 3-0, with one commissioner recused, to grant a continuance request and resume the Notice of Intent hearing for the athletic fields project at a future meeting.

fayville-memorial-park-improvements.name: Fayville Memorial Park improvements
fayville-memorial-park-improvements.description: Planning, community outreach, and design improvements for Fayville Memorial Park, including splash pad features and parking capacity.
fayville-memorial-park-improvements.status: Recreation staff are consulting town counsel and the Community Preservation Committee regarding potential Article 97 restrictions and parking layout options near the reservoir.

flagg-turnpike-hydrant-relocation.name: Flagg Road and Route 9 hydrant relocation
flagg-turnpike-hydrant-relocation.description: Relocation of a frequently struck fire hydrant and removal of scenic road stone wall at Flagg Road and 361 Turnpike Road.
flagg-turnpike-hydrant-relocation.status: The Planning Board voted 5-0 to approve removing 10 feet of scenic stone wall on Flagg Road to allow DPW to relocate a fire hydrant away from vehicle strikes.

fy27-road-paving-contracts.name: FY27 road paving and sidewalk contracts
fy27-road-paving-contracts.description: Procurement and contract awards for fiscal year 2027 DPW road paving and sidewalk maintenance.
fy27-road-paving-contracts.status: The Select Board voted 5-0 to award FY27 DPW contracts for road paving and sidewalk improvements.

fy27-school-operating-budget.name: FY27 school operating budget
fy27-school-operating-budget.description: Operating budget planning, class size staffing, and reserve funding for the Southborough K-8 public schools for fiscal year 2027.
fy27-school-operating-budget.status: The School Committee voted to request that the Select Board allocate an additional $105,485 received in Chapter 70 state education aid into the town's Special Education Stabilization Fund.

fy28-operating-budget.name: FY28 operating budget
fy28-operating-budget.description: Operating budget planning, multi-year deficit forecasting, and consideration of a Proposition 2 1/2 operational override for fiscal year 2028.
fy28-operating-budget.status: The Board of Health rescheduled its vote on its departmental operating budget request to a special meeting on October 20, 2026, after the item was not posted in time.

glow-sobo-holiday-lighting.name: Glow SoBo holiday lighting
glow-sobo-holiday-lighting.description: Funding and municipal installation of holiday lighting displays and kickoff event for the Tricentennial.
glow-sobo-holiday-lighting.status: The Library Board of Trustees unanimously approved the Tricentennial Committee's plan to install exterior decorative holiday lighting and permanent outdoor power outlets at the Southborough Library.

hopkinton-water-connection.name: Hopkinton MWRA water connection
hopkinton-water-connection.description: Proposed intermunicipal agreement to convey MWRA water to the town of Hopkinton through Southborough's distribution system.
hopkinton-water-connection.status: The Select Board reviewed the status of intermunicipal agreement negotiations to convey MWRA water to Hopkinton, noting upcoming needs for independent engineering peer review and special counsel. The board plans to vote on appointing independent special counsel at a future meeting.

housing-and-food-enforcement-policies.name: Housing and food health code enforcement policies
housing-and-food-enforcement-policies.description: Board of Health standardized enforcement procedures, violation correction timelines, and fee schedules for housing and food establishments.
housing-and-food-enforcement-policies.status: The Board of Health reviewed draft violation enforcement policies and fee schedules, with refined violation correction timelines scheduled for review on September 15, 2026.

kallander-field-repairs.name: Kallander Field turf repairs
kallander-field-repairs.description: Scoping, vendor pricing, and DPW coordination for repairing turf and playing surface conditions at Kallander Field.
kallander-field-repairs.status: The Recreation Commission received an $8,000 to $9,000 repair estimate from the original turf installer and scheduled a formal presentation and decision for June 2026.

kratom-retail-ban.name: Statewide kratom ban and local enforcement
kratom-retail-ban.description: Local Board of Health enforcement and retail monitoring following the state's Schedule I temporary ban on kratom.
kratom-retail-ban.status: Board of Health staff reviewed local retail compliance following Massachusetts designating kratom as a Schedule I substance, finding only one local retailer carrying the product.

landfill-environmental-assessment.name: Southborough landfill environmental assessment
landfill-environmental-assessment.description: Environmental risk assessment, private well testing, and potential municipal water line extension regarding contamination from the Southborough landfill.
landfill-environmental-assessment.status: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend Town Meeting approval of Article 7 to fund water connections and service lines for two homes near the Parkerville Road landfill from water retained earnings.

latisquama-road-errant-golf-balls.name: Latisquama Road errant golf balls
latisquama-road-errant-golf-balls.description: Safety concerns and mitigation options regarding errant golf balls striking residential properties on Latisquama Road from the Southborough Golf Club.
latisquama-road-errant-golf-balls.status: The Golf Committee reviewed abutter concerns about errant golf balls striking homes on Latisquama Road near the 7th tee and agreed to consult a golf architect on potential hole redesign options.

library-book-drop-repair.name: Library book drop concrete repair
library-book-drop-repair.description: Repair and funding of damaged concrete beneath the Southborough Library book drop and clarification of municipal maintenance responsibilities.
library-book-drop-repair.status: The Library Board of Trustees scheduled repair of the concrete platform beneath the book drops for October 3, 2026, temporarily relocating book drops to the front lawn.

library-cpa-signage.name: Library CPA commemorative signage
library-cpa-signage.description: Design and wording of commemorative plaques crediting Community Preservation Act funding for Southborough Library restoration projects.
library-cpa-signage.status: The Community Preservation Committee approved plaque phrasing crediting Southborough residents, and invoices have been submitted for reimbursement.

library-parking-lot-repaving.name: Library parking lot repaving
library-parking-lot-repaving.description: Capital planning, DPW coordination, and town warrant sponsorship for repaving the Southborough Library parking lot.
library-parking-lot-repaving.status: Library trustees and town facilities confirmed that parking lot repaving is deferred from the FY28 capital cycle to future town capital plans due to costly drainage and engineering constraints.

mcauliffe-hearing-room-av.name: McAuliffe Hearing Room audiovisual upgrades
mcauliffe-hearing-room-av.description: Hardware, camera framing, and video conferencing upgrades for hybrid public meetings in the McAuliffe Hearing Room at the Town House.
mcauliffe-hearing-room-av.status: Front desk screens were lowered and microphone upgrades began to improve visibility and sound in the McAuliffe Hearing Room, while the Municipal Technology Committee continues monitoring resident feedback.

metrowest-recc-borrowing.name: MetroWest RECC borrowing authorization
metrowest-recc-borrowing.description: Short-term borrowing authorization of up to $12.5 million to bridge state grant funding for the MetroWest Regional Emergency Communication Center.
metrowest-recc-borrowing.status: The Select Board voted 4-1 to approve up to $12.5 million in short-term borrowing authority to bridge state grant funding for regional dispatch center construction.

municipal-grants-management-policy.name: Municipal Grants Management Policy
municipal-grants-management-policy.description: Town oversight and approval procedures governing municipal grant applications, match funding, and operational liabilities.

municipal-health-insurance-reform.name: Municipal employee health insurance reform
municipal-health-insurance-reform.description: Adoption of MGL Chapter 32B Sections 21-23 and collective bargaining with the Public Employee Committee to modify municipal health insurance plans.
municipal-health-insurance-reform.status: The Select Board voted 5-0 to adopt MGL Chapter 32B Sections 21 through 23 to begin expedited negotiations with the Public Employee Committee on health plan design changes.

national-grid-vegetation-plan.name: National Grid FY27 vegetation management plan
national-grid-vegetation-plan.description: Annual review and approval of National Grid's tree pruning and vegetation management plan along town distribution circuits.
national-grid-vegetation-plan.status: The Planning Board voted 3-0 and the Tree Warden concurred to approve National Grid's FY27 vegetation management plan, with tree pruning along town distribution circuits scheduled to begin within weeks.

native-plant-landscape-regulations.name: Native plant landscape regulations
native-plant-landscape-regulations.description: Proposed Planning Board site plan rules and regulations mandating native plantings and invasive species management.
native-plant-landscape-regulations.status: The Planning Board voted 5-0 to adopt new Native Landscape Regulations mandating native species and prohibiting neonicotinoids for site plan review projects.

neary-school-building-project.name: Neary School building project
neary-school-building-project.description: Feasibility, design, and renovation or replacement planning for Neary Elementary School.
neary-school-building-project.status: The Elementary School Building Committee voted 3-1 to eliminate Option 4 and 4-0 to direct consultants to focus on Options 1, 3, and a $15 million baseline scope. Consultants will deliver draft presentation materials on October 13 ahead of an October 15 committee meeting and the October 17 Town Meeting presentation.

neary-school-roof-replacement.name: Neary School roof replacement
neary-school-roof-replacement.description: Proposed borrowing and debt exclusion to replace the failing roof and fund ADA upgrades at Neary Elementary School.
neary-school-roof-replacement.status: Combined low bids totaled approximately $2.8 million and construction is scheduled to begin in late June, with summer childcare relocated to Finn School and substantial completion targeted for late August 2026.

opeb-funding-strategy.name: OPEB liability funding strategy
opeb-funding-strategy.description: Actuarial valuation, liability modeling, and long-term trust contribution strategy for the town's Other Post-Employment Benefits.
opeb-funding-strategy.status: The Select Board reviewed actuarial valuations of the town's OPEB liability and directed the actuary to model several future contribution scenarios.

parkerville-road-utility-pole.name: Parkerville Road utility pole petition
parkerville-road-utility-pole.description: Petition by National Grid and Verizon to install an additional utility pole between poles 101 and 102 on Parkerville Road.
parkerville-road-utility-pole.status: The Conservation Commission closed the public hearing and voted 5-0 to issue an Order of Conditions for the replacement and installation of utility distribution poles along Parkerville Road and Lynbrook Road.

peninsula-trail-phase-2.name: Peninsula Trail Phase 2
peninsula-trail-phase-2.description: Scope, wetland crossing design, and construction funding for Phase 2 of the Peninsula Trail.
peninsula-trail-phase-2.status: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to advance the $217,318 CPA funding article to Special Town Meeting as written, while the Advisory Committee unanimously opposes the appropriation due to cost. The Trails Committee will present the article as drafted on October 17 without offering a floor amendment.

personal-property-tax-exemption.name: Personal property tax exemption threshold
personal-property-tax-exemption.description: Proposed Town Meeting warrant article to raise Southborough's personal property tax exemption threshold from $1,500 to $2,500.
personal-property-tax-exemption.status: The Advisory Committee updated its Special Town Meeting report text to clarify that raising the tax exemption threshold to $2,500 would exempt 22 accounts with a combined assessed value of $40,100.

police-drone-program.name: Police Department drone program
police-drone-program.description: Proposed acquisition of a five-year police drone program package funded through unspent municipal personnel funds.
police-drone-program.status: The Municipal Technology Committee voted 4-0 to recommend approval of the Police Department's five-year drone program under a phased deployment featuring pre-deployment verification, an initial pilot, and formal reviews after 90 days and 12 months.

presidential-fisher-waterline-looping.name: Presidential and Fisher Road waterline looping
presidential-fisher-waterline-looping.description: MWRA loan funding and construction to connect dead-end water mains under CSX railroad tracks along Presidential Drive and Fisher Road.
presidential-fisher-waterline-looping.status: The Select Board voted unanimously to authorize a $1 million interest-free MWRA loan application to fund the waterline looping project under CSX railroad tracks.

rescinding-unissued-borrowing.name: Rescission of unissued borrowing authorizations
rescinding-unissued-borrowing.description: Proposed Special Town Meeting warrant article to rescind unused borrowing authorizations for completed capital projects, including Breakneck Hill and the Neary School study.
rescinding-unissued-borrowing.status: The Advisory Committee refined its warrant report to explain that Article 6 cancels unused debt authority for completed projects rather than returning cash ahead of Special Town Meeting.

reserve-fund-transfer-policy.name: Reserve Fund transfer policy
reserve-fund-transfer-policy.description: Advisory Committee policy setting standard procedures, executive board oversight, and statutory criteria for departmental Reserve Fund transfer requests.
reserve-fund-transfer-policy.status: The Advisory Committee revised its reserve fund transfer guidelines to require vetting by the town administrator and prohibit reimbursement of previously paid or encumbered expenses. A clean working draft is being prepared for final approval at a future meeting.

route-9-495-gateway-study.name: Route 9 and I-495 gateway corridor study
route-9-495-gateway-study.description: A joint $150,000 planning and infrastructure study with Westborough evaluating economic development, zoning, and infrastructure along the Route 9 and I-495 corridor.
route-9-495-gateway-study.status: The Wastewater Study Committee paused further meetings and consultant hiring while awaiting the state's Community One Stop for Growth grant announcement in October 2026.

route-9-wastewater-infrastructure.name: Route 9 wastewater infrastructure plan
route-9-wastewater-infrastructure.description: Planning, site evaluation, and District Improvement Financing for wastewater collection and treatment along the Route 9 corridor.
route-9-wastewater-infrastructure.status: The Wastewater Study Committee agreed to focus planning on a modular sewer collection design along the south side of Route 9 and deferred warrant articles to the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting. Committee representatives will participate in an informational consultation with MassDEP in late September 2026.

ruby-estates-subdivision.name: Ruby Estates subdivision
ruby-estates-subdivision.description: Six-lot residential subdivision along Lampson Drive off Mount Vickery Road.
ruby-estates-subdivision.status: The Planning Board voted 5-0 to accept a surety agreement backed by a bond exceeding $300,000 and released all six subdivision lots from the covenant.

rural-cemetery-water-tower.name: Rural Cemetery stone water tower restoration
rural-cemetery-water-tower.description: Proposed structural evaluation, restoration, and Community Preservation Act funding for the historic stone water tower in Rural Cemetery.
rural-cemetery-water-tower.status: The Community Preservation Committee formally deferred the water tower restoration funding application to the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting round due to consultant workloads.

sarsenstone-way-coc.name: Sarsenstone Way Certificate of Compliance
sarsenstone-way-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review and archival records search for the 1970s Sarsenstone Way subdivision under DEP file 290-100.
sarsenstone-way-coc.status: The Conservation Commission voted 5-0 to approve a full Certificate of Compliance for the subdivision under DEP File 290-100 after archival Department of Public Works records confirmed that required roadway and drainage infrastructure had been built.

scenic-road-tree-removals.name: DPW scenic road tree removals
scenic-road-tree-removals.description: Tree Warden and DPW hearings and approvals to trim or remove public shade trees along designated scenic roads.
scenic-road-tree-removals.status: Following a joint hearing with the Tree Warden, the Planning Board approved the removal of four trees and the trimming of one tree on scenic roads.

school-bus-transportation-operations.name: School bus transportation and technology
school-bus-transportation-operations.description: Bus operations, safety tracking technologies, and vendor performance oversight with contractor NRT.
school-bus-transportation-operations.status: The district reported improved bus route reliability with contractor NRT and plans to meet in June to negotiate contract penalties for delayed technology rollouts.

school-food-service-contract.name: School food service contract renewal
school-food-service-contract.description: Contract administration, financial performance, and annual renewals for district food services with Whitsons Culinary Group.
school-food-service-contract.status: The School Committee voted unanimously to extend its food service contract with Whitsons Culinary Group for the 2026-2027 school year.

senior-tax-work-off-policy.name: Senior Tax Work-Off policy and slot allocation
senior-tax-work-off-policy.description: Eligibility regulations and position allocations for Southborough's Senior Tax Work-Off property tax abatement program.
senior-tax-work-off-policy.status: The Select Board voted unanimously to adopt a revised Senior Tax Work-Off Policy and set the program's allocation at 40 slots.

southborough-golf-club-audubon-plan.name: Southborough Golf Club Audubon management plan
southborough-golf-club-audubon-plan.description: Consultant RFP and environmental management plan to achieve Audubon International certification for the Southborough Golf Club.
southborough-golf-club-audubon-plan.status: The Golf Committee voted unanimously to pay $500 in Audubon International dues and authorized up to $4,500 from its revolving fund to bridge the funding gap for a consultant's certification proposal.

southborough-golf-club-irrigation.name: Southborough Golf Club irrigation replacement
southborough-golf-club-irrigation.description: Planning, value engineering, and Community Preservation Act funding for replacing the irrigation system at Southborough Golf Club.
southborough-golf-club-irrigation.status: The Golf Committee agreed by consensus to present its CPA funding article as written at the October 17 Special Town Meeting without seeking floor amendments.

sta-unit-c-contract.name: Southborough Teachers Association Unit C contract
sta-unit-c-contract.description: Three-year collective bargaining agreement between the Southborough School Committee and the Southborough Teachers Association covering Unit C support staff.
sta-unit-c-contract.status: The School Committee voted 5-0 to approve a three-year collective bargaining agreement with the Southborough Teachers Association covering Unit C administrative assistants and educational support professionals.

stewardship-committee-structure.name: Stewardship Committee structure and merger proposal
stewardship-committee-structure.description: Deliberation over committee appointments and a proposal to merge the Stewardship Committee with the Open Space Preservation Commission.
stewardship-committee-structure.status: The Select Board voted 4-1 to amend the committee charge to add a fourth at-large member and 5-0 to appoint Freddie Gillespie to the seat through June 2027.

stormwater-enterprise-fund.name: Stormwater enterprise fund
stormwater-enterprise-fund.description: Proposed Town Meeting warrant article to establish a municipal enterprise fund for stormwater management accounting and future funding.
stormwater-enterprise-fund.status: The Advisory Committee adjusted its report language for Article 5 ahead of Special Town Meeting, emphasizing that establishing the enterprise fund structure does not implement any fees without future Town Meeting approval.

street-tree-planting-program.name: Street tree planting pilot study
street-tree-planting-program.description: A pilot study and planting program to evaluate street canopy cover and identify replacement tree planting locations.
street-tree-planting-program.status: The Planning Board voted 5-0 to approve a $5,500 expenditure for Davey Resource Group to conduct an initial street tree planting pilot study evaluating 10 to 15 streets.

town-budget-process-policy.name: Town budget process policy
town-budget-process-policy.description: Draft municipal policy formalizing timelines, board responsibilities, and procedures for constructing the annual town omnibus budget.
town-budget-process-policy.status: The Select Board reviewed a proposed budget policy defining board roles and timelines, agreeing to seek further input from Town Counsel and the Department of Revenue.

town-common-fence-restoration.name: Town Common fence restoration
town-common-fence-restoration.description: Repair and restoration of the historic fence and railings at the Town Common funded by the Community Preservation Act.
town-common-fence-restoration.status: A contract was executed with Kneeland Construction, with a multi-department coordination meeting scheduled for June 29, 2026.

town-forest-footbridge.name: Town Forest Eagle Scout footbridge
town-forest-footbridge.description: Construction materials, permitting, and approvals for an Eagle Scout footbridge project in the Town Forest.
town-forest-footbridge.status: The Stewardship Committee voted 4-0 to approve the use of pressure-treated lumber for an Eagle Scout footbridge project in the Town Forest after reviewing environmental findings from the Conservation Commission.

town-governance-study.name: Town governance structure study
town-governance-study.description: A consultant-led study evaluating Southborough's municipal government structure, town manager authority, and committee organization.
town-governance-study.status: Consultant Bill Keegan presented an initial overview of Southborough's governance model, town manager authority, and committee structures to the Select Board as the municipal structure study gets underway.

town-satisfaction-survey.name: 2026 Town Satisfaction Survey
town-satisfaction-survey.description: Design, public outreach, and execution of the townwide resident satisfaction survey conducted by the Municipal Technology Committee.
town-satisfaction-survey.status: The Municipal Technology Committee and Affordable Housing Trust refined survey questions and finalized community outreach plans for the 2026 survey, which is scheduled to run from October 1 through November 30, 2026.

town-website-redesign.name: Town website redesign
town-website-redesign.description: Redesign of the municipal website with vendor CivicPlus and consolidation of standalone departmental pages.
town-website-redesign.status: Contract and module discussions with CivicPlus for the town website upgrade remain scheduled to begin around November 2026, targeting implementation in early 2027.

transfer-station-fees-and-regulations.name: Transfer station fees and regulations
transfer-station-fees-and-regulations.description: Department of Public Works updates to transfer station sticker pricing, outside hauling costs, and operational rules for disposal.
transfer-station-fees-and-regulations.status: The Select Board voted unanimously to continue participating in the 35-member municipal consortium negotiating bulk disposal rates with WIN Waste ahead of the contract expiration in December 2027.

tricentennial-firefighters-muster.name: 2027 Tricentennial Firefighter's Muster
tricentennial-firefighters-muster.description: Organization of a regional firefighter's muster and antique hand tub demonstration at Woodward School in July 2027.
tricentennial-firefighters-muster.status: Eight antique fire apparatus teams have confirmed participation for the 2027 muster, and organizers are preparing site and parking layouts ahead of the next committee meeting.

tricentennial-first-day.name: First Day 2027 celebration
tricentennial-first-day.description: Planning for Southborough's January 1, 2027 Tricentennial kickoff celebration featuring family activities, a drone show, and a bonfire.
tricentennial-first-day.status: A contract was executed for a 200-drone light show for January 1, 2027, and committee leaders scheduled a site walk to inspect potential bonfire locations ahead of a November 17 student artwork deadline.

tricentennial-heritage-day-parade.name: 2027 Tricentennial Heritage Day Parade
tricentennial-heritage-day-parade.description: Planning for an expanded Heritage Day Parade in October 2027 featuring marching units, community floats, and a historic cannon.
tricentennial-heritage-day-parade.status: The parade working group is reviewing route and staging options and coordinating with public safety officials ahead of future parades.

tricentennial-street-banners.name: Tricentennial commemorative street banners
tricentennial-street-banners.description: Permitting and installation of celebratory banners on utility poles across Southborough's historic villages.
tricentennial-street-banners.status: Town administration is continuing utility permitting paperwork to install celebratory banners on utility poles across town.

tricentennial-summer-nights.name: Summer Nights 2027 music festival
tricentennial-summer-nights.description: Expansion of the annual Summer Nights community event into a multi-act music festival for the 2027 Tricentennial.
tricentennial-summer-nights.status: Organizers are finalizing stage specifications and coordinating event layouts with police, fire, and recreation departments for the August 21, 2027 music festival, ahead of an accessibility grant application deadline on October 18, 2026.

tricentennial-time-capsule.name: Tricentennial time capsule
tricentennial-time-capsule.description: Selection, preservation, and public placement of a commemorative time capsule for Southborough's 300th anniversary.
tricentennial-time-capsule.status: The Tricentennial Committee continues coordinating collection protocols offline for items to be placed inside the 300th anniversary time capsule.

trottier-finn-expansion-studies.name: Trottier and Finn expansion feasibility studies
trottier-finn-expansion-studies.description: Proposed Special Town Meeting articles to study expanding Trottier and Finn schools to reconfigure grade levels and take Neary School offline.
trottier-finn-expansion-studies.status: The School Committee, Select Board, and Advisory Committee all recommend defeating Articles 2 and 3 to study expanding Trottier and Finn schools at the March 2, 2026 Special Town Meeting, warning that additions would be required to prevent severe programming cuts.

trottier-school-roof-replacement.name: Trottier Middle School roof replacement
trottier-school-roof-replacement.description: Proposed funding and MSBA grant reimbursement to replace the roof at Trottier Middle School.
trottier-school-roof-replacement.status: The School Committee incorporated the Trottier Middle School roof project into the FY27 capital plan ahead of an MSBA funding determination.

two-family-zoning-amendment.name: Two-family dwelling zoning amendment
two-family-zoning-amendment.description: Proposed zoning bylaw amendment for Town Meeting to eliminate the requirement that a single-family dwelling exist for two years before converting to a two-family home.
two-family-zoning-amendment.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted unanimously to support the proposed bylaw amendment as drafted, while the Advisory Committee finalized report language recommending against approval ahead of the October 17 Special Town Meeting.

well-and-septic-regulations.name: Well and septic regulation amendments
well-and-septic-regulations.description: Board of Health regulations governing private well testing, swimming pool setbacks, and subsurface sewage disposal systems.
well-and-septic-regulations.status: Following a public hearing, the Board of Health voted unanimously to adopt updated well and septic regulations requiring separation of septic design and installation roles, guaranteed access for repairs, a 25-foot pool setback, and mandatory pre-transfer well testing.
